_season_note: Issue 21 (Standard Weekly, 7 August 2026). The In Practice season 'Technical strategy under uncertainty' was CUT SHORT at two issues (19, 20) under the v3.5 'cut the season short rather than drag' rule - Phase 1 ran nine queries on the theme and surfaced only normative framework writing, which the explicit disqualifiers rule out. New season opens: 'Handling reorgs and ambiguous mandates' (v1.35 managing-across-and-upwards pool), week 1 = Ben Balter on twenty-five reorgs in thirteen years at GitHub. THE LEADERSHIP READ WAS OMITTED - a deliberate call, not thin material. The v1.35 long-form variety rule caps AI-primary pieces at one across In Practice / Outside In / Leadership Read, and every Leadership Read candidate in the pool was AI-primary alongside an AI-primary Outside In. The spec permits dropping the third long-form section rather than squeezing. last_leadership_read is therefore UNCHANGED at 'The Pragmatic Engineer'. ISSUE 22 MUST CARRY A LEADERSHIP READ - this is the first consecutive skip and the limit is two. Ludicity ('AI mania is eviscerating global decision-making', 18 July) is the standing candidate and has never appeared in leadership_read_history; Canva / Rob Giglio is the second, dropped from Issue 21 only on the source-diversity cap. DEEP DIVE TRIGGER: consecutive_non_deepdive reaches 3 at this issue - the trigger fires at Issue 22. Lead was EU AI Act Article 50, which took the rolling-4 leads to all four operational concerns. The regulator scope-conditional test (v1.32) was worked in full and PASSED on the horizontal-technology-regulation reading; the ECB's 31 October deadline for its 110 supervised banks was the negative control and FAILED, sized to one On the Radar line. Binding facts carried forward unchanged: no shared cause has ever been published for the 27 July UK multi-bank degradation - simultaneity is documented, causation is not, and Faster Payments the rail did NOT fail. The 'July 2026 AWS mega-outage' remains UNVERIFIED and was demoted for a fourth consecutive issue. AWS ME-CENTRAL-1 / ME-SOUTH-1 remain OPEN on the AWS Health Dashboard with AWS's last public update dated 30 April 2026; the dashboard could not be re-verified this week and the copy says nothing stronger. The agentic-payments deep-dive cluster stays retired. Phase 3 verification was unusually load-bearing this run: it withdrew four Klarna claims the run plan had carried from a commentator source (including a '5,000 to 3,500 support headcount' figure that is actually total company headcount), corrected the Anthropic inference-hooks mechanism, and pinned the Article 50 penalty to Article 99(4) plus the SME lower-of clause at 99(6). The 2 December 2026 marking backstop comes from the Digital Omnibus on AI, not the original Act. Phase 5 caught two epistemic reframings Phase 4's self-scan missed (its lexical scan found the two canonical patterns and stopped) and one misapplied Cooley URL; both fixed before publication, along with a bespoke .compare-table.cmp-wide modifier that existed only to defeat the documented 2-column cap. .rabbit-hole and .by-the-numbers were folded into weekly-template.html so future runs stop re-porting them by hand.
_retired_threads_note: The 'payments-sector engineering org shape under AI attribution' thread seeded at Issue 20 is RETIRED. Two consecutive issues brought no new in-window movement, and the sector aggregate could not be verified: the Block figure is internally contradictory across sources (reported as both 'close to half' and 'nearly 40%' of headcount) and the Mastercard and PayPal figures remain search-result reported only. None of those figures appeared anywhere in Issue 21. Visa appeared once, in Other News, carrying a single cross-issue throughline sentence on the $2.4bn BioCatch acquisition.
